node-1.label: Shortness of breath and fatigue on exertion for one week

node-2.label: Patient is an 84-year-old man with medical history of permanent atrial fibrillation on warfarin therapy for more than 15 years, hypertension, and obstructive sleep apnea.

node-3.label: Patient used a walker for ambulation and had a mechanical fall two years ago with a T12 vertebral fracture requiring orthopedic intervention, with no falls since then.

node-4.label: Medications included metoprolol, amlodipine, and over-the-counter acetaminophen.

node-5.label: Physical examination: blood pressure 140/80 mm Hg, pulse irregular at 130 beats/min, respiratory rate and oxygen saturation normal, jugular venous pressure estimated at 10 cm, heart sounds demonstrated variable intensity of S1 and S2, no murmurs, gallops, or rubs appreciated, remainder unremarkable.

why.why: Expert analyses reinforce that the modest BNP elevation and the imaging findings of tamponade physiology favor cardiac tamponade over decompensated heart failure. The radiologist also explicitly states that normal oxygenation argues against heart failure. ECG-confirmed AF remains a background rhythm but does not explain the full clinical picture, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

The radiologist’s analysis notes that normal oxygenation argues against pulmonary embolism, which aligns with the normal respiratory rate, normal oxygen saturation, and unremarkable physical examination already in the graph. Acute PE remains unlikely, so confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.1.

The current belief explicitly states that anemia appears secondary rather than primary, and both experts interpret the declining hemoglobin as evidence of bleeding into the pericardium rather than a primary hematologic disorder. Anemia is therefore a secondary phenomenon, and confidence is reduced from 0.15 to 0.1.

Expert analyses emphasize normal oxygenation and the unremarkable examination, both of which argue against an acute pulmonary disease exacerbation. No new supporting evidence emerged, so confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

node-10.label: Echocardiogram reveals pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology

node-11.label: CT shows high-density complex pericardial effusion with hepatic vein reflux and ventricular compression

node-12.label: BNP is 393 ng/L, only modestly elevated

node-15.label: Leukocytosis is present on laboratory testing

node-17.label: Patient has cardiac tamponade from hemorrhagic pericardial effusion

why.why: Both expert analyses independently confirm the echocardiography and CT findings of a high-density complex pericardial effusion with tamponade physiology, including hepatic vein reflux and ventricular compression. The elevated INR of 7.7, declining hemoglobin, and long-term warfarin use are explicitly cited as supporting a hemorrhagic etiology. The radiologist further notes that even without detailed Doppler respiratory variations, the available imaging and laboratory evidence sufficiently confirm tamponade physiology. Confidence is therefore increased from 0.85 to 0.92.

node-18.label: Cardiac tamponade due to warfarin-related hemopericardium

why.why: The Laboratory Physician and Radiologist both explicitly favor warfarin-related hemopericardium: INR 7.7 on warfarin and falling hemoglobin strongly support bleeding into the pericardial space, and the high-density effusion on CT is consistent with blood. This refinement of the tamponade diagnosis is more strongly supported than the other hemorrhagic etiologies, so confidence is increased from 0.85 to 0.90.

node-19.label: Cardiac tamponade due to malignant pericardial effusion

why.why: Both experts strongly support warfarin-related hemopericardium given the INR of 7.7 and long-term warfarin use, and there is no evidence of malignancy in the belief or expert analyses. Malignant pericardial effusion remains a low-probability alternative, so confidence is reduced from 0.08 to 0.05.

node-20.label: Cardiac tamponade due to uremic pericardial effusion

why.why: No evidence of renal failure or uremia is present in the belief or expert analyses, and the hemorrhagic effusion is best explained by warfarin-related bleeding. Uremic pericardial effusion remains very unlikely, so confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.03.

node-21.label: Cardiac tamponade due to post-traumatic pericardial effusion

why.why: There is no recent trauma (the fall was two years ago), and both experts support warfarin-related bleeding as the mechanism. Traumatic hemopericardium remains extremely unlikely, so confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.
